tools.name: list_tasks
tools.label: Checking your to-do list
tools.description: List the open items on the team's to-do list.

tools.name: add_task
tools.label: Adding it to your to-do list
tools.description: Add one item to the team's to-do list for the person you are talking to.

title.description: Short, plain description of what needs doing.

tools.name: complete_task
tools.label: Marking it done
tools.description: Mark one to-do item done, by its id (from list_tasks) or by words from its title.

match.description: Words from the item's title, when you have no id.

tools.name: calendar_upcoming
tools.label: Looking at your calendar
tools.description: List upcoming events on the Google Calendar of the person you are talking to.

tools.name: add_calendar_event
tools.label: Putting it on your calendar
tools.description: Put one event on the Google Calendar of the person you are talking to. Invites nobody. It waits in the Approvals tab and is added only when they tap Approve; in practice mode it is shown, never added.

tools.name: search_email
tools.label: Looking through your email
tools.description: Find recent emails in the Gmail of the person you are talking to. Returns sender, subject, date and a short preview.

tools.name: draft_email
tools.label: Writing the email
tools.description: Send one email from the Gmail of the person you are talking to. It waits in the Approvals tab and is sent only when they tap Approve; in practice mode it is shown, never sent.

tools.name: imessage_search
tools.label: Looking through your texts
tools.description: Read the iMessages and texts of the person you are talking to, synced from their own Mac. Newest first. Filter by words in the message, by a contact's name, phone or email, and by how many days back.

query.description: Words in the message, e.g. 'inspection'. Leave out to get recent messages.

contact.description: Part of the contact's name, phone number or email, e.g. 'Brad'.

tools.name: browser_open
tools.label: Opening the website
tools.description: Open a public website in their own web browser and read it. Returns the page as text, with each button, link and box named like e12. Never needs approval.

tools.name: browser_read
tools.label: Reading the page
tools.description: Read the page that is open in the browser again, with fresh element names.

tools.name: browser_scroll
tools.label: Scrolling the page
tools.description: Scroll the open page down (or up) and read it.

tools.name: browser_back
tools.label: Going back a page
tools.description: Go back to the previous page and read it.

tools.name: browser_request_access
tools.label: Asking to work on this site
tools.description: Ask the owner's go-ahead to click, type and sign in on the site that is open (or the site named). Files one approval in the Approvals tab for the whole task; once approved you can act on that site for 30 minutes. Payments, purchases and deleting anything still get their own approval.

task.description: One plain sentence: what you will do on the site, e.g. 'Sign in and download the October statement'.

site.description: Optional site address, when the page isn't open yet.

tools.name: browser_click
tools.label: Clicking
tools.description: Click one element on the open page, by its name from the page text (e.g. e12). Needs the task approved for this site first.

tools.name: browser_type
tools.label: Typing
tools.description: Type text into one box on the open page (replacing what is there), optionally pressing Enter after. Never for passwords: use browser_login. Needs the task approved for this site first.

tools.name: browser_press
tools.label: Pressing a key
tools.description: Press one key on the open page. Needs the task approved for this site first.

tools.name: browser_login
tools.label: Signing in
tools.description: Sign in on the open page with the login they saved for this site in Settings. You never see the password. Open the site's sign-in page first. Needs the task approved for this site first.

tools.name: browser_ask_person
tools.label: Asking you to take over
tools.description: Hand the browser to them when the page needs something only they can do: signing in when there's no saved login, a verification code or two-step prompt, a 'prove you're human' check, or a choice that is theirs to make. The browser window in this chat switches to 'Action needed' with your reason and a Take over button. Use it as soon as you hit such a page instead of stopping or describing the problem; then tell them what to do and wait for them.

reason.description: One plain sentence shown on the card: what they need to do, e.g. 'Sign in to Google, then tap I'm done.'

tools.name: connect_google
tools.label: Getting the Google connect button ready
tools.description: Ask the app to show its own 'Connect your Google account' button in this chat. Use it when something needs their Google and it is not connected. Never write a link yourself.
